options.text: Controlling upstream pollution to protect downstream water

options.misconception: it selects "Managing each parcel independently" because it fits a common but mistaken reading, rather than "Controlling upstream pollution to protect downstream water"

questions.explanation: Watershed management controls upstream actions to protect downstream water. Parcels are not independent because water connects them. At first glance tempting, "Treating the watershed as arbitrary" looks reasonable but does not hold up: it denies the natural unit. A reasonable-sounding guess, "Managing each parcel independently" is a seductive distractor: it selects "Managing each parcel independently" because it fits a common but mistaken reading, rather than "Controlling upstream pollution to protect downstream water". Easy to pick on a quick read, "Ignoring upstream land use" fails on closer inspection: it denies downstream effects.
questions.hint: Upstream actions affect downstream water.
